# Reference Data Tables

The lookups that detections and automation read at run time. If these are wrong or stale, automation either can't act or acts on the wrong thing. Source: `catalog/data-tables.yaml`.

## How tables are maintained

**Scripts build, agents propose, humans approve, automation reads.**

| Who | Does | Never does |
|---|---|---|
| **Deterministic script** | Pulls from the authoritative sources on a schedule, applies fixed rules, writes the table, flags diffs and stale rows | Guess. Anything the rules can't classify goes to the agent |
| **AI agent** | Classifies what the rules couldn't, researches new items, drafts owner questions, explains diffs | Write to a table directly. It submits proposals |
| **Human** | Approves proposals and periodically re-attests | Hand-maintain anything a script can pull |
| **Automation** | Reads the runtime copy at action time | Act on a missing or stale row without falling back to the safe default |

Rules for every table:
- [ ] **Tightening is automatic, loosening needs a human.** A script or agent may move a host from C to B or remove an exception on its own; moving to C or adding an exception needs approval.
- [ ] **Every row has a source and a last-seen or last-reviewed date.** Rows past their refresh window count as missing.
- [ ] **Every table has a safe default** for missing rows, and automation uses it.
- [ ] **Health is monitored:** last refresh time, row count change, and % of hosts/identities with no row. A table that stops refreshing is an alert.
- [ ] **Every table has one store of record with a change history** (who changed what, when, why). Automation reads a runtime copy (SIEM lookup, EDR tag, IdP group) kept in sync from it.

## Tier 1 dependencies: automation reads these before acting, so build them first

### Asset containment tiers (T-01)

Which hosts automation may isolate (A), contain-lite (B), or never isolate (C).

- **Sources:** EDR inventory, AD / IdP device objects, cloud inventory, CMDB if trusted, running services and logon telemetry
- **Script:** Pull all hosts from the EDR. Workstations become A by OS type. Tier C is set by signal (DC role, hypervisor, IdP connector, security tooling, backup, OT segment). Everything else is B. Push the tier as an EDR tag.
- **AI agent:** Classify servers the rules can't (what is this box, from services, listening ports and logons); draft the yes/no question for the app owner.
- **Human:** App owners answer the isolate yes/no question; security approves any move to C. Quarterly re-attestation for B and C.
- **Refresh:** daily · **Safe default:** Missing or unknown = B (contain-lite + page).
- **Columns:** hostname, tier, role, owner, reason, source, confirmed_date, last_seen
- **Used by:** Build asset containment tiers (can / cannot auto-isolate) (F-02), Isolate host via EDR (ACT-01), Isolate host at the network layer (ACT-02), Decoy files and canary credentials on endpoints and shares (A-01), Credential theft behavior on an endpoint (A-03), Machine-speed recon burst (A-13), Ransomware precursors (A-15)

### Identity containment tiers (T-02)

Which identities automation may disable/revoke on its own vs. needs approval.

- **Sources:** identity source of truth (AD / Entra / Okta), HR feed, IdP admin roles, service account OUs and naming, sign-in telemetry
- **Script:** Join IdP users with HR. Humans in HR = A. Admin roles, executives = B. Break-glass, service accounts, sync/connector accounts = C. Accounts not in HR become "suspected non-human" for review.
- **AI agent:** Classify suspected service accounts from behavior (no MFA, logs on only from servers, fixed schedule) and find an owner from logon hosts and group memberships.
- **Human:** Approve every move to C; quarterly review of the C list.
- **Refresh:** daily · **Safe default:** Missing = B (revoke sessions + page; disable needs a click).
- **Columns:** identity, tier, type (human/service/agent/break-glass), owner, reason, last_reviewed
- **Used by:** Build identity containment tiers (F-03), Revoke sessions and tokens (ACT-03), Disable account (ACT-04), Reset password and MFA methods (ACT-05), MFA fatigue burst followed by an approval (A-06), One identity fanning out fast (A-09)

### Containment exceptions and allowlists (T-03)

Every suppression in one place (sanctioned dump tools, scanners, backup jobs, pentest IPs, IT jump hosts).

- **Sources:** requests from IT and security, tuning during the 2-week recommend-only period
- **Script:** Expire entries past their end date and alert the owner 14 days before. Report the entries that suppressed something this week.
- **AI agent:** When a recommend-only rule fires on something benign, draft the narrowest possible exception (hash + host + account, not a wildcard).
- **Human:** Security approves every entry. No entry without an owner, a reason and an expiry (max 12 months).
- **Refresh:** daily (expiry check) · **Safe default:** Not on the list = no exception.
- **Columns:** rule, match (hash/path/account/host/ip), owner, reason, created, expires
- **Used by:** Decoy files and canary credentials on endpoints and shares (A-01), Credential theft behavior on an endpoint (A-03), One identity fanning out fast (A-09), Workstation-to-workstation admin protocols (A-10), Machine-speed recon burst (A-13), Ransomware precursors (A-15), Exfiltration tool on a server (A-16)

### Decoy and canary registry (T-04)

Where every decoy file, canary account and canary key lives, so a hit is instantly recognized and decoys stay healthy.

- **Sources:** deployment job output, AD (canary accounts), cloud IAM (canary keys)
- **Script:** Deploy decoys, record path and hash per host, and check weekly that every decoy still exists, canary accounts are still disabled for logon and audit (SACL) is still on.
- **AI agent:** Suggest new decoy placements that fit each environment (fake configs and scripts that look native).
- **Human:** Approve decoy content and placement policy once.
- **Refresh:** weekly health check · **Safe default:** Any access to a path or account in the registry = Tier 1 hit.
- **Columns:** type, location, host_or_account, deployed, last_verified
- **Used by:** Decoy files and canary credentials on endpoints and shares (A-01), Canary AD accounts (honey user, honey SPN) (A-02), Canary cloud access keys (A-11)

### Approved remote access, RMM and tunneling tools (T-05)

Anything not on this list triggers the unapproved remote access tool detection.

- **Sources:** IT, EDR software inventory, procurement/contracts
- **Script:** Stack remote access tool executions fleet-wide and diff against the list.
- **AI agent:** Research newly seen tools (vendor, purpose, abuse history) and recommend approve or remove.
- **Human:** IT owner approves additions.
- **Refresh:** weekly diff · **Safe default:** Not on the list = unapproved.
- **Columns:** tool, approved_use, hosts_or_groups, owner, reviewed
- **Used by:** Unapproved remote access or tunneling tool (A-14), Cut third-party and remote access (M-03)

### Network segments and quarantine paths (T-06)

Subnet to site/type mapping (workstation, server, DMZ, OT, VPN, guest), plus how to network-quarantine a host in each segment.

- **Sources:** IPAM, DHCP scopes, firewall and NAC config, cloud VPC/VNet config
- **Script:** Pull DHCP scopes and cloud network ranges; flag IPs seen in telemetry that fall in no known segment.
- **AI agent:** Propose segment type for unknown ranges from the hosts seen in them.
- **Human:** Network owner confirms segment types and the quarantine method per segment.
- **Refresh:** weekly · **Safe default:** Unknown segment = no network-layer quarantine; page instead.
- **Columns:** cidr, site, type, quarantine_method, owner
- **Used by:** Isolate host at the network layer (ACT-02), EDR tampering corroborated by a second signal (A-04), Workstation-to-workstation admin protocols (A-10), Asset containment tiers (T-01)

### Change and maintenance windows (T-07)

Suppress tamper and silent-sensor alerts during planned work, and only then.

- **Sources:** change management system, EDR upgrade schedules
- **Script:** Pull approved changes (host, start, end) into a lookup the automation checks.
- **AI agent:** Match an alert to an open change ticket and say so in the case.
- **Human:** none beyond normal change approval
- **Refresh:** every 15 minutes · **Safe default:** No matching change = no suppression.
- **Columns:** change_id, hosts_or_scope, start, end, owner
- **Used by:** EDR tampering corroborated by a second signal (A-04), Logging or security tool disabled (A-08), Edge device admin or config change (D-12)

### Cloud accounts and allowed regions (T-15)

Which cloud accounts, subscriptions and regions are in use, so activity elsewhere is a Tier 1 signal.

- **Sources:** cloud organization APIs, billing
- **Script:** Pull accounts/subscriptions and the regions with resources; diff weekly.
- **AI agent:** none
- **Human:** Cloud owner confirms the region allowlist.
- **Refresh:** weekly · **Safe default:** Region not in the list = disallowed.
- **Columns:** provider, account_or_subscription, owner, allowed_regions
- **Used by:** Cloud principal acting from outside its expected environment (A-12), Cloud enumeration burst or new admin grant (D-09)

## Tier 2 context: detections and the triage agent need these

### Privileged identities (T-08)

Every admin across AD, IdP, cloud, EDR, SIEM and SaaS, so a new one is a detection and an alert on one is higher priority.

- **Sources:** AD privileged groups, IdP admin roles, cloud role assignments, EDR/SIEM console admins, key SaaS admin roles
- **Script:** Snapshot all privileged assignments daily; diff = new privilege alert.
- **AI agent:** Explain each diff (who granted it, ticket, is it expected).
- **Human:** Quarterly access review.
- **Refresh:** daily · **Safe default:** n/a (used for context and alerting)
- **Columns:** identity, system, role, granted_by, granted_date
- **Used by:** New identity persistence (no-malware access) (D-06), Phishing-resistant MFA for admins (H-01), Lock down the EDR console itself (H-06), Mass session revocation and privileged password reset (M-01)

### Service account baselines (T-09)

Where each service account normally logs on and from what; the basis for fan-out and anomaly detections without drowning in noise.

- **Sources:** logon telemetry (30 days), AD
- **Script:** Build per-account set of source and destination hosts and logon types over 30 days, rolling.
- **AI agent:** Triage logons outside the baseline.
- **Human:** none
- **Refresh:** daily · **Safe default:** No baseline = alert, not auto-contain.
- **Columns:** account, usual_sources, usual_destinations, logon_types, last_built
- **Used by:** One identity fanning out fast (A-09), Kerberoasting / credential spraying (D-07), Identity containment tiers (T-02)

### Internet exposure inventory (T-10)

What's reachable from the internet, who owns it, and whether it has known-exploited vulnerabilities.

- **Sources:** external attack surface scan, cloud public IPs and load balancers, DNS zones, firewall NAT rules, vulnerability scanner, CISA KEV feed
- **Script:** Weekly external scan and cloud pull; diff against last week; join with vulnerability scan results and the KEV feed.
- **AI agent:** Triage new exposures (what is it, who likely owns it) and summarize KEV hits with urgency.
- **Human:** Owner confirms each new exposure is intended.
- **Refresh:** weekly (KEV join daily) · **Safe default:** New and unconfirmed exposure = alert.
- **Columns:** asset, ip_or_hostname, port_service, owner, known_exploited_vulns, first_seen
- **Used by:** Know what's exposed to the internet (F-09), Server process spawning a shell (exploited service) (D-04), Edge device admin or config change (D-12), Blast radius sweep (I-03)

### AI agent and MCP inventory (T-11)

Every AI agent, MCP server and AI connector, with its identity, permissions and owner; anything not listed is unapproved.

- **Sources:** EDR (agent processes, MCP config files, IDE extensions), OAuth app grants in the IdP/M365/Google, low-code agent platform admin APIs, procurement
- **Script:** Weekly discovery sweep across all sources; diff against the approved list.
- **AI agent:** Research new agents/MCP servers (publisher, requested permissions, data reach) and recommend approve or remove.
- **Human:** Owner and security approve additions; anything that can write or execute needs a named owner.
- **Refresh:** weekly · **Safe default:** Not on the list = unapproved (triage detection fires).
- **Columns:** agent, type, identity, can_write_or_execute, tools_and_data, owner, logs_in_siem, approved
- **Used by:** Inventory AI agents, their identities and their tools (F-10), Kill switch for an AI agent (ACT-11), AI agent doing something it shouldn't (D-13), New or unapproved MCP server, agent or AI connector (D-14), Least privilege for AI agents (H-07)

### Trusted locations and egress IPs (T-12)

Corporate egress IPs, VPN ranges and sanctioned cloud/proxy IPs, so sign-in and cloud detections can tell inside from outside.

- **Sources:** firewall NAT config, VPN/ZTNA config, IdP named locations
- **Script:** Pull and sync to IdP named locations and SIEM lookups.
- **AI agent:** none
- **Human:** Network owner confirms quarterly.
- **Refresh:** weekly · **Safe default:** Unknown IP = untrusted.
- **Columns:** cidr, type, owner
- **Used by:** Risky sign-in or session anomaly (D-02), Cloud principal acting from outside its expected environment (A-12)

### VIPs and high-risk users (T-13)

Executives, finance approvers, IT admins and their assistants get faster triage and B-tier identity handling.

- **Sources:** HR org chart, finance approval roles
- **Script:** Pull titles and roles from HR monthly.
- **AI agent:** none
- **Human:** Security confirms the list quarterly.
- **Refresh:** monthly · **Safe default:** n/a
- **Columns:** identity, reason
- **Used by:** Risky sign-in or session anomaly (D-02), Identity containment tiers (T-02)

## Later: the remaining 20%

### Fleet behavior baselines (T-14)

What is normal across the fleet (drivers, persistence entries, server outbound destinations, business file-sharing domains), so new things stand out.

- **Sources:** EDR / Sysmon telemetry, DNS and proxy logs
- **Script:** Stack counts across the fleet weekly; anything seen on fewer than N hosts or new this week goes to the diff.
- **AI agent:** Triage the weekly diff (LOLDrivers, signer reputation, destination reputation).
- **Human:** none beyond triage escalations
- **Refresh:** weekly · **Safe default:** New = goes to the agent, never auto-contained on its own.
- **Columns:** type, value, signer_or_owner, host_count, first_seen
- **Used by:** New persistence on a server (D-05), New kernel driver not seen in the fleet baseline (D-08), Exfiltration tool on a server (A-16)
